title: The Industrial Revolution

cards.h: Why did a rainy island change how the whole world works?
cards.b:
Around 1760, one small country began making things with machines and coal instead of hands and muscle. Within a century, the world had factories, railways and slums.

That island was Britain. The question is why.

Thomas Newcomen built an early steam engine in 1712. James Watt greatly improved it from the 1760s-70s. Spinning machines such as Hargreaves's jenny and Arkwright's water frame (1760s) multiplied output.

The Liverpool and Manchester Railway opened in 1830, with Stephenson's engines. Manchester grew from a town into a vast 'cotton city'. Factories ran on fixed hours. Time itself got stricter.

Trade in raw cotton relied on slave plantations in the American South.

Workers, including young children, laboured 12-14 hours in noisy mills. Cities lacked clean water and drains, and cholera and typhus spread. Slow reforms followed, such as the Factory Act of 1833, which limited children's hours.

In the long run, living standards rose, but for several decades many people were worse off.

Historians argue. Ideas: coal near the surface, high wages that made machines worth building, an overseas empire for markets and raw materials, secure property rights and a culture of tinkering. Kenneth Pomeranz (The Great Divergence, 2000) stressed coal and colonies. No single cause is accepted by all.

Myth: Luddites (1811-16) smashed machines because they hated progress.Fact: they were skilled textile workers protesting low pay and loss of their trade. Machine-breaking was a way to bargain. The government sent more troops against them than it had sent to fight Napoleon in some years; the law made machine-breaking punishable by death in 1812.

Five things to remember

  1. Britain began industrialising around 1760.
  2. Coal, steam and cotton were central.
  3. Factories brought both wealth and hardship.
  4. Why Britain is debated.
  5. India's textile industry suffered; railways came in 1853.

Think about it

  • Who gained and who lost in the early factory age?
  • What makes people smash machines?
